newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Share dumping seen persisting on Nigerian bourse.
newsitem.headline: Share dumping seen persisting on Nigerian bourse.

text.p: Dumping of blue chip stocks will persist at the Nigerian stock market next week as investors continue to revalue securities, dealers said on Friday.
The all-share index closed at 8415.74 on Friday, down from 8440.90 on Thursday, setting the mood for the coming week, they said.
"The market currently considers most blue chips overpriced and investors are selling to cut their losses," one said. Caught in the middle are conglomerates, oil and food manufacturing companies.
Flour Mills, which has risen consistently in recent weeks, fell sharply on Friday by 80 kobo to 17.50 naira in speculative trade.
Nigerian Tobacco Company (NTC) also shed 10 kobo on negative market perception, to close at 2.30 naira.
Traders said it had lost 30 percent of its value since the beginning of the year as smuggling and poor quality brands rob it of its former blue-chip status.
Lever Brothers was down 20 kobo to 27.10 naira while PZ Industries and UAC were each 10 kobo weaker at 26.70 naira and 15.10 naira, respectively.
Nigerian Breweries also fell 10 kobo to 18.25 naira but Guinness retained its new found attraction, rising by a similar amount to 7.40 naira.
Positive sentiments shot United Bank for Africa (UBA) 15 kobo up to 12.70 naira.
Wema Bank and NAL Merchant Bank rose five kobo apiece to 3.90 naira and 8.50 naira, respectively.
The unimpressive performance of health care firm Smithkline Beecham recently cost it a 30 kobo slide to 5.65 naira, dealers said.
African Petroleum at 54.90 naira and Agip at 16.70 naira were the petroleum sector's main losers.
Traders said investors were shunning the troubled sector on account of poorer profit outlooks and because of Nigeria's fuel supply hiccups.
